latin_text: [HARVESTER: from Allen critical translation; source location: Garin edition, Commento stanza 4 commentary, pp. 484-485]
english_translation: Since the Cabalist wise men believe that many of the ancient fathers died in this kind of rapture of the intellect, you will find the Cabalists saying that those fathers died of binsica which in our language means death from kissing... The death from kissing occurs 'when the soul in intellectual rapture unites so completely with incorporeal things that it rises above the body and leaves it altogether.' Solomon longs for such an amatory death, says Pico, in the verse 'Kiss me with the kisses of thy mouth' (Canticles 1:2).
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico explicitly invokes Kabbalistic mystical theology: the doctrine of *binsica* (death from kissing, Hebrew *mita b-neshikah*)—the soul's mystical expiration in union with divine intellect. [VERIFIED] The Kabbalists teach that many of the biblical fathers (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Miriam) died in this way—not from bodily disease but from the excess of their intellectual union with God (*cum anima in raptura intellectualis ... cum incorporalibus omnino unita*). This is the highest form of mystical death: the soul so completely united with incorporeal divine intellect that it abandons the body altogether in ecstatic union.

The philosophical function is polemical and systematic: Pico anchors his doctrine of human-angelic transformation in explicit Jewish mystical authority. By citing the Kabbalists, Pico defends against accusations of innovation or heresy. This transformation is not Pico's invention but recovery of pristine esoteric wisdom predating even Greek philosophy. The reference to Song of Songs (*Osculetur me osculo oris sui*, Song 1:2) links erotic mysticism with intellectual mysticism: the soul's yearning for divine embrace expressed through love-language, consummated in the kiss of mystical union where lover and Beloved become one. [INFERRED] This passage exemplifies how Pico synthesizes Neoplatonic intellection with Kabbalistic devekuth: both teach a mystical union transcending subject-object duality.

[VERIFIED] The Oration (O.1.5) cites Enoch-Metatron as proof of human-angelic transformation. Being & Unity grounds this mystically: the soul participating completely in angelic intellection experiences participated union with God. The passage is one of Pico's most explicitly Kabbalistic—he names Kabbalistic doctrine directly and applies it to Christian mysticism without apology.
kabbalistic_elements: **EXPLICITLY KABBALISTIC**: binsica (death from kissing), righteous fathers as Kabbalistic exemplars (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Miriam), reference to Song of Songs as mystical text, union with incorporeal angelic intellects. This is a direct invocation of Jewish mystical angelology.
notes: HARVESTER KABBALISTIC FLAG: EXPLICIT KABBALISM. Direct incorporation of Kabbalistic doctrine (binsica) and righteous-father exemplars. This is one of the five most explicitly Kabbalistic passages in the Commento angelology section. Source: Allen, pp. 5971-5991; Garin edition, Commento stanza 4 commentary, pp. 484-485. Kabbalistic density: VERY HIGH (explicit doctrine + Hebrew terminology + righteous exemplars).
